pr_summary: Decimal128 arithmetic optimization - avoid unnecessary promotion to Decimal256 for operations that can safely remain in Decimal128. The fix adds precision/scale checks before promoting Decimal128 operations to Decimal256, and optimizes spark_decimal_div to use native i128 arithmetic when precision allows instead of BigInt.
environment_management: Rust toolchain via rustup (rust-version = 1.75 minimum), JDK 8/11/17 for JVM side, Maven for Java/Scala build
patch_file_cues: Decimal128 arithmetic operations (Plus, Minus, Multiply, Modulo)
Precision and scale calculations (p1, s1, p2, s2)
BigInt vs native i128 arithmetic decision based on precision bounds
test_file_cues: planner.rs has inline tests module at line 1829
scalar_funcs.rs has tests in sub-modules (hex.rs, unhex.rs)
platform_constraint_evidence: CI runs on ubuntu-latest container with amd64/rust image
Linux shared library output (.so) in Makefile targets
Cross-compilation support for Linux x86_64 and aarch64
No Windows-specific dependencies or MSVC requirements
Project builds and tests successfully on Linux containers
notes: This is a multi-language project (Rust + Java/Scala) with Rust native code as a Spark accelerator. The fix.patch modifies Rust code for Decimal128 optimization. The project uses Cargo for Rust builds and Maven for JVM builds. Tests can run on Linux x86-64 containers. The Rust minimum version is 1.75. Key dependencies include Apache DataFusion, Arrow, and Parquet. The fix avoids unnecessary Decimal256 promotion when Decimal128 precision is sufficient.
